checks: The underlying volume is summed d-volume on a finite set of integer fibers. At a regular support level, nearby sections projected to its hyperplane lie in shrinking neighborhoods of the zero-volume support section. Thus the bounded parallel-section profile is continuous at all required levels, including supporting and exterior ones.

On the fiber at z the threshold is b−a(b)(z−m), so its derivative is −s_z+a′(z−m)s_z. Stationarity gives zero total first base moment, and the moments of the two closed sides are −T and +T because the central term is zero.

The proper central trace contains a point in the interior of K_m, which provides the anchor for the exact section theorem. The masses s_z and its derivative-section masses are the same because e is unit. Both closed sides count the central mass and have sections bounded between γ_d S and S.

Adding the indicated signed integrals yields W′_±=−S_±. All volumes and corrections are absolutely continuous, so one may integrate on every subinterval. For fixed tilt the correction vanishes, and the derivative hypotheses holding almost everywhere suffice. A zero-mass terminal cap in that fixed-tilt case gives the asserted remaining-cap composition.

dependencies.hypotheses: At each eligible level choose any central section point x_0 in the own interior. Set u=e in the stationary oblique section theorem. Its integer stationarity and null-boundary hypotheses are exactly those of this sweep, and its masses agree fiber by fiber.

overlap.comparison: The accepted two-sided cap first variation yields the fiber derivative once the moving threshold is substituted. It does not give the closed-side scalar section bounds or the integrated moving-tilt correction.

readability: The terminal-cap conclusion applies to the fixed-tilt almost-everywhere formulation. At an empty terminal cap the central trace need not be proper.
